title: Solid state defect emitters with no electrical activity
abstract: Point defects may introduce defect levels into the fundamental band gap of the host semiconductors that alter the electrical properties of the material. As a consequence, the in-gap defect levels and states automatically lower the threshold energy of optical excitation associated with the optical gap of the host semiconductor. It is, therefore, a common assumption that solid state defect emitters in semiconductors ultimately alter the conductivity of the host. Here we demonstrate on a particular defect in 4H silicon carbide that a yet unrecognized class of point defects exists which are optically active but electrically inactive in the ground state.
